key_insight: Large language models can meaningfully assist cancer registry abstraction, with the best models reaching about 0.8 F1 on several common registry variables but performing less well on exact date extraction.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLMs could speed up registry data entry and reduce manual workload, while still requiring careful human oversight for harder fields and high-stakes use.
method: Benchmarked five foundation LLMs in zero-shot prompting
Abstracted eight cancer registry variables from clinical reports
Evaluated 5,939 patients across seven cancer types
evidence_signal: The study compared model outputs against hospital cancer registry ground truth across thousands of patients and multiple variable types, showing stronger performance for low-cardinality fields and weaker exact accuracy for dates.
watch_item: Real-world deployment should be cautious because performance varied by variable complexity, and date extraction remained imperfect even for the best models.
paper_title: Large language models for cancer registry abstraction: a real-world evaluation across models, variables, and cancer types
